9.0.0.en: Beyond Jordan: what is meant is the west bank of the river Jordan.

9.0.1.en: The great sea: the Mediterranean Sea.

9.0.2.en: The Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites and the Perizzites: Canaanite tribes.

9.0.3.en: After the victory over Jericho and Ai, a general tension arose among the kings of the main cities lying west of the river Jordan as far as the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, in all the regions, mountains and plains alike.

9.1.0.en: The kings of the lands lying west of the Jordan agreed to unite together and fight the children of Israel so that it would be easy to defeat them.

9.1.1.en: Do not be troubled if the wicked agree against you, however strong or numerous they appear, for they are nothing before the power of God that is with us. Present your need before God and make supplication to Him, and you will stand firm and no one will be able to overcome you.

9.2.0.en: Gibeon: its meaning is a hill, and it is a city located nine kilometers north of Jerusalem and strongly fortified (Map 1). The Lord had designated for His people seven tribes with whom they were not to make a covenant but to devote them to destruction because of their many evils (Deut 7:

9.2.1.en: 1-2) They are the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and the inhabitants of Gibeon were of the Hivites, and they had heard of the victory of the Jews over Jericho and Ai and the killing of their inhabitants, so they were very afraid and devised a plan to escape from the hands of the children of Israel.

9.3.2.en: Bottles: leather vessels for carrying water or wine.

9.3.5.en: The Gibeonites deceived the Jews, pretending that they had come from a far country, and they took old sacks and put in them dry, crumbled bread and old wineskins full of holes, and they bound up the holes so that they were stopped, and put on old sandals and tattered clothes, and loaded their donkeys and came to the Jews.

9.4.0.en: The Jews were camped at Gilgal, which is near Jericho (ch. 4:19), and the Gibeonites asked them to make a peace treaty, and the Jews hesitated lest they be of the inhabitants of the nearby land that the Lord had promised them as an inheritance and whose people He had commanded to be devoted to destruction.

9.5.0.en: When Joshua asked them about their origin and where they dwelt, they lied to him, claiming that they had come from a far country, believing in the power and greatness of God when they heard of the ten plagues that the Lord brought on the Egyptians and the drowning of Pharaoh and his army in the sea.

9.6.0.en: They also heard of the victory of the Jews over the kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og, east of the Jordan, and Og dwelt in his capital Ashtaroth. The lands of these two kings were east of the Jordan and were taken by the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh after they defeated these two kings and their armies (Deut 2, 3).

9.7.0.en: The Gibeonites said, "Our elders, when they heard the news of your power and your victories, told us to take provision with us and travel to you and ask you to make a covenant with us, and we will be your servants. And the proof that we dwell in a place very far from you is that our bread which we took as provision when we set out was hot, and now it has become not only dry but crumbs, and our wineskins, which were new, have burst from the length of the journey, and our sandals have worn out from much walking."

9.7.1.en: Be careful in your life, so that the devil does not deceive you with his tricks, and in order to discover them, examine whether the thought or matter presented to you brings you nearer to God, leads you to edification and gives you rest and peace, and make sure of that through prayer. If it is so, it is from God, and if it is the opposite, it is from Satan, however logical it appears, because the devil interprets reality with his evil thoughts to deceive you and take you away from God.

9.8.s.en: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

9.8.0.en: The Jews and Joshua took of the Gibeonites' food and ate with them, as a sign of peace and covenant not to harm, and they swore to them by the name of the Lord to confirm that. This was done without their praying to God and asking His opinion, exactly as they did when they fought Ai without taking God's opinion, and they were defeated.

9.9.0.en: After the covenant was made, the Gibeonites returned to their country, and after three days the children of Israel discovered that they lived near them, and perhaps they learned this from some merchants, or some of the neighboring Canaanite inhabitants informed on them because they were angry with them for their covenant with the children of Israel.

9.10.0.en: The children of Israel journeyed on the road to the country of the Gibeonites and reached it after three days, which means that it is about 39 kilometers from them, and they could not fight their four cities mentioned, because they had made a covenant with them. And the people murmured against Joshua and against the leaders for making this covenant, either because some of them held fast to God and were distressed at the lack of prayer and of taking His opinion before the covenant, or because others wanted to take the spoils of these lands after fighting them and defeating them.

9.11.0.en: The leaders declared that there could be no turning back after the oath, as it says in (Ps 15:4) that whoever knows God swears to his own hurt and changes not, that is, does not go back on his oath even if he suffers harm or loss, otherwise harm would come on them from the Lord. And we shall see afterward in (2 Sam 21:1, 2) that when Saul dealt treacherously with the Gibeonites and killed them, there was wrath from God against him, and accordingly the leaders told them that it was not possible to fight them or kill them.

9.12.0.en: The leaders sentenced them to work at gathering wood and drawing water for all the people and for the tent of meeting. And Joshua reproached them for deceiving him by claiming that their country was far away when it was near. By this the Gibeonites became slaves to the children of Israel, working at tasks that helped them.

9.13.0.en: Joshua cursed them and declared to them his previous judgment, that is, that their curse is that they became slaves to the children of Israel, and they excused themselves that they were very afraid when they learned that the Lord had promised Moses and the people this land and the destruction of its inhabitants, so they did this trick to save themselves and their country from destruction, and they left their case to Joshua to do with them as he saw fit. This shows that they believed in the power of the God of the children of Israel, like Rahab.

9.14.0.en: In the place which he should choose: the place of the house of the Lord, which is the tent of meeting or the temple of Solomon.

9.14.1.en: Joshua judged as he judged and did not allow the people to kill them, and they continued to carry out the sentence and served the people and the tent of meeting until the days of the writing of the book of Joshua, and their service to the temple continued after it was built.

9.14.2.en: Afterward they were called the Nethinim, that is, those dedicated to the service of God, since they were helpers to the Levites in gathering wood and carrying the water needed by the house of the Lord.

9.14.3.en: The Gibeonites believed in the power of God, so they received life and became servants of the house of God. And you, by faith, receive eternal life, and God favors you with serving Him and you enjoy fellowship with Him.

9.14.4.en: The victory over the five kings

10.0.s.en: (1) The five kings' war against Gibeon

10.0.0.en: Adonizedec: a name meaning lord of righteousness.

10.0.1.en: Jerusalem: Ur means light, and Shalem means peace, so its meaning is light of peace, and it is commonly called the city of peace; it is present-day Jerusalem (al-Quds) and is located northwest of the Dead Sea at a distance of 14 miles. When Adonizedec king of the city of Jerusalem, the largest city in the group of five cities west of the Jordan, which lies beyond Gibeon and was exposed to Joshua's attack upon it, heard that Joshua had killed the people of Jericho and the people of Ai, and heard also of the peace of the Gibeonites with Joshua, which would weaken his position and that of his neighbors before Joshua, since Gibeon lies in the midst of their cities.

10.1.0.en: The king of Jerusalem was afraid because the city of Gibeon was a great city like the cities ruled by kings and called royal cities, that is, great and principal, and all its men were mighty in war, but it feared the children of Israel and made peace with them.

10.2.0.en: Hebron: present-day Hebron (al-Khalil), located 30 kilometers south of Jerusalem.

10.2.1.en: Jarmuth: a city about 25 kilometers west of Jerusalem.

10.2.2.en: Lachish: a fortified city located in the possession of the tribe of Judah.

10.2.3.en: Eglon: a city in the possession of the tribe of Judah, located 15 km northeast of Gaza (Map 3). The Amorites: the strongest of the Canaanite peoples.

10.2.4.en: Adonizedec moved to form an alliance of four kings with him from the nearby cities so that they might begin to fight Joshua before he surprised them with war. Their plan began with declaring war on Gibeon, the ally of Joshua, to draw him into war with them, and so five Amorite kings gathered to fight Gibeon. Gaza Map (3)

10.3.0.en: The mountain: the mountains lying southwest of Jerusalem.

10.3.1.en: Mighty men of valour: strong men of war.

10.3.2.en: The Gibeonites cried out fervently to their ally Joshua to hurry to their help in repelling that attack of the five, so Joshua moved with his mighty army from Gilgal to their rescue and hastened toward Gibeon.

10.3.3.en: The five kings in their alliance were thinking of defeating Joshua, but God used their alliance to deliver them together as spoil to Joshua and give him victory over them. Your God is able to turn the plots of the wicked into a blessing for you and a cause of salvation and victory, for He turns evil into good.

10.4.s.en: (2) Joshua's victory and the help of heaven for him

10.4.0.en: The Lord reassured Joshua that He had indeed delivered these five kings into his hand and that he would defeat them, and He said "I have delivered them" in the past tense, because since God has commanded, His word will surely come to pass.

10.5.1.en: Joshua exerted himself and marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon, a distance of about 39 kilometers, to attack the five kings suddenly and so prevail over them. His moving during the night was something the enemies did not expect, and it shows faithfulness on his part and also skill in war.

10.6.0.en: Azekah: a city located 18 kilometers west of Jerusalem.

10.6.1.en: The going up to Beth-horon: a projecting rock located 18 kilometers northwest of Jerusalem.

10.6.2.en: Makkedah: a city located south of Jerusalem (Map 3). God discomfited the five kings, and they were greatly afraid of the children of Israel, and it became easy for Joshua to strike them with a great slaughter and chase them from before Gibeon to the going up to Beth-horon, to Azekah and Makkedah.

10.7.0.en: Hailstones: balls of ice reaching 15 cm in diameter that can break or kill any human they strike.

10.7.1.en: The Lord cast down upon them from heaven heavy hailstones, which killed more of them than those who died by the sword of the children of Israel.

10.8.0.en: Ajalon: a city located at a distance of 21 kilometers west of Jerusalem.

10.8.1.en: While Joshua was fighting the five kings gathered before Gibeon and his victory over them had begun, the sun was about to set, so he asked God that the sun continue to shine so that he might complete his victory over the kings, and he commanded the sun to remain shining over Gibeon and the moon over the valley of Ajalon, which is a city located beside Gibeon. People sometimes see the sun and the moon at the same time at sunset, and this shows the authority of the children of God over nature.

10.9.0.en: The book of Jasher: a book in poetry and prose that records the important events in the history of the Jews.

10.9.1.en: The midst of heaven: the height and middle of the sky.

10.9.2.en: God answered, and Gibeon continued to be lit until Joshua overcame the enemies ... and this event was recorded in the book of Jasher. Thus the day was prolonged until Joshua completed his victory over the kings, and this wonderful answer of God was one of the greatest miracles and a proof that God fights with Joshua and his people. This means that God the Almighty stopped the whole universe for the sake of His son Joshua who made supplication to Him, and He stopped any side effects of the sun's remaining for a long period over the earth, so no harm occurred, and this stopping was for a whole day. Historians of that era have mentioned the existence of a long day, such as Herodotus the Greek, the writer of the history of Egypt, and also the historians of China.

10.9.3.en: God supports you as His son in ways you accept and ways you cannot imagine. Trust in Him with all your heart, keep His commandments, and do not fear the ferocity of the enemy.

10.10.s.en: (3) The pursuit of the enemies and the killing of their kings

10.10.0.en: After the victory the people returned to Gilgal, but the five kings fled after the defeat of their armies and hid in a cave at Makkedah.

10.11.0.en: The hindmost of them: the rear of the fleeing army.

10.11.1.en: When Joshua learned of this, he commanded the people to close the mouth of the cave upon them by placing great stones against it, and not to occupy themselves with them for now but to be content with confining them and guarding them lest they escape, while the people continued pursuing their enemies and smiting the rear of their armies in their flight to prevent them from returning to hide in their cities and renewing their strength to resume the war, because God had decreed their destruction.

10.12.0.en: Those that remained: those who separated from the army and scattered to flee.

10.12.1.en: Move his tongue: speak with blame.

10.12.2.en: This continued until the great victory was achieved, and none of the enemies escaped except those who succeeded in fleeing and hiding in the fortified cities. And all the people returned victorious to Joshua at Gilgal, with none of the inhabitants of the land able to harm them.

10.13.0.en: Then Joshua commanded that the cave be opened and the five kings brought out of their confinement, and they brought them out.

10.14.0.en: They bound the five kings and cast them on the ground before Joshua, and Joshua called the commanders of the army to put their feet on the necks of those five kings as a sign of their victory over them, and they did so. And Joshua asked them not to fear in the future but to be encouraged by God, who will always give them victory over their enemies. Joshua did not mean by this gloating or rage and revenge against the kings, but he meant the following:

10.14.1.en: 1- Proclaiming the authority of God and His crushing of all the wicked, however great they are, and showing the worthlessness of the power of their pagan gods.

10.14.2.en: 2- Encouraging his army to tread down and triumph over all the peoples of Canaan.

10.14.3.en: 3- Frightening and disturbing all the kings of Canaan who would hear this news.

10.15.0.en: Joshua killed the five kings with the sword and hanged them on wooden trees until evening, and commanded that their bodies be taken down from the trees at sunset, being content with what had happened so as not to be excessive in punishment, as the Law prescribed (Deut 21:22, 23); and hanging on a tree had been a symbol of shame and disgrace from ancient times. Then they buried them in the cave in which they had hidden and closed it with stones, to the day of the writing of the book.

10.15.1.en: Do not hinder yourself from positive work by being occupied with negative things. Striving for spiritual progress and constructive work are more important and more lasting in benefit than being occupied with side matters that hinder a person.

10.16.s.en: (4) The subjugation of the cities of the south

10.16.0.en: After Joshua finished subduing the central sector of the region west of the Jordan, he moved on his way to the southern sector, and took Makkedah and killed its king and devoted its people to destruction as he did to Jericho.

10.17.0.en: Libnah: a city located 18 km southwest of Jerusalem.

10.17.1.en: Lachish: a city located south of Libnah.

10.17.2.en: Gezer: a city located 30 km west of Jerusalem (Map 3). Then he came to Libnah and did the same to it, then to Lachish to the south and besieged it two days, then Gezer, and did the same to both. Thus he killed all who were in these lands and their kings, and conquered and took possession of them.

10.18.0.en: Eglon: a city located 15 km northeast of Gaza.

10.18.1.en: Hebron: present-day Hebron (al-Khalil), located 30 km south of Jerusalem (Map 3). Then he repeated the same action at Eglon and Hebron and the cities belonging to them, and they killed the new king of Hebron who had been set up after the king who was killed with the five kings (vv. 23, 26), and he killed all who were in these lands and took possession of them.

10.19.0.en: Debir: a city near Hebron, which was the seat of religious learning among the Canaanites (Map 3). Then he returned to Debir and took it despite the greatness of its religious standing among the Canaanites, and did the same to it, killing its king and all who were in it and taking possession of it.

10.20.0.en: All the country of the hills: the mountainous lands that were in the portion of the tribes of Judah and Ephraim. The south: the Negev, which is the south of the Promised Land.

10.20.1.en: The vale: the lowlands on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

10.20.2.en: The springs: the sloping lands lying at the foot of the mountains.

10.20.3.en: Thereby Joshua took possession of all the hill country lying in the portion of Judah and Ephraim, and the vale and the slopes of the mountains, and killed and devoted to destruction all their kings and their people, according to the Lord's command.

10.21.0.en: At one time: that is, he did not stop the war and took possession of these lands in a short time by the power of God.

10.21.1.en: Kadesh-barnea: located on the southern border of Canaan.

10.21.2.en: Goshen: located in the possession of Judah, south of Hebron.

10.21.3.en: Joshua took possession of the lands lying from the border of the land of Canaan in the south to Gaza in the west and all the land of the region that Judah inhabited, and this was done at one time with God's help to Joshua and to the people, and then Joshua returned with all the people to Gilgal.

10.21.4.en: As Joshua achieved many victories by the miraculous power of God, be confident that God is able to work with you so that you triumph over all the wars of the devil, however strong he is.

10.21.5.en: Kings of the north, east and west of Canaan
